name: small-molecule-tractability-review
description: Assembles small-molecule druggability evidence for one protein target — retrieved precedent and computed tractability as two separate, never-averaged axes — and returns a single JSON dossier with provenance on every number.
runtime_notes: Custom-tool handlers run in the calling process, not the sandbox (lib/claude-managed-agent.ts consumeUntilEndTurn -> executeCustomTool). That is what lets this agent reach the paperclip binary and the fpocket/mdpocket conda stack, neither of which the sandbox can install.

The sandbox is NOT network-restricted: environments.retrieve() on 'mvp-shared' reports config.networking.type == 'unrestricted'. A structure-fetch custom tool was drafted and then dropped because RCSB egress from the sandbox is proven, and a redundant fetch path would be a second untested route to the same data.

ROUTED, NOT APPLIED — scripts/deploy.ts:279 zips each skill bundle with `zip -r <zip> <dir>` and no exclusions, so 14 __pycache__/*.pyc files upload to the Skills API with absolute laptop paths baked into co_filename. Fix is `["-r", zipPath, dirName, "-x", "*__pycache__*", "-x", "*.pyc"]`. Shared starter infrastructure — owner must apply.

ROUTED, NOT APPLIED — the shared 'mvp-shared' environment has no `packages` block, so numpy/gemmi are absent from the sandbox. Not expressible from this manifest: getOrCreateEnvironment() in lib/claude-managed-agent.ts posts only {name} and never reads the manifest. Adding packages is a separate environment update in shared runtime code.
agent/tools/druggability-dossier.ts passes an explicit timeoutMs of 45 minutes. runTask defaults to 10, which a Modal pocket scan (function timeout 1800 s plus cold start) can exceed on its own.

managed/druggability-dossier/.claude/skills/structure-select/neighbour_precedent.py carries an absolute contributor path as its --env-file argparse default. The tool handler always passes an explicit --env-file derived from repoRoot instead, and hands it an empty temp file when the repo has no .env, so the default is never reached. The script is owned elsewhere and was not edited.

CLAUDE.md was NOT edited by this compile — it is held by another agent — but outcome mode requires three changes to it (a canonical sandbox output path, a shell-to-tool bridging table, and a declaration of the axes no tool can fill). Those were written out as a routed patch. Its hash below is therefore a pre-patch baseline: the next recompile will see a mismatch that is this compile's routed change landing, not a founder hand-edit.

Running `bun run fix` repo-wide during this compile reformatted managed/druggability-dossier/pipeline.html and eight fixtures/*.json files owned by other parallel sessions. All nine were verified to still parse and to be byte-complete; the change was formatting only. Use `bunx ultracite fix <paths>` on owned files only.
CLAUDE.md hash re-baselined after landing compile patches CM-A/B/C (sandbox output path, tool bridge table, rule 13). Not a founder hand-edit.

RUBRIC/VALIDATOR ALIGNMENT: rubric.md was rewritten against validate_dossier.py read fresh, and the counts in the old rubric were wrong — the validator now carries 16 rule functions emitting 17 violation codes (not 13/14), with three added since: DRUGGABILITY_LOAD_BEARING (rule 4.0), VOLUME_NOT_PRIMARY (rule 4a) and SITE_INCONSISTENT (rule 4b/2b). Criteria 1-17 of the rubric are now exactly those codes in registry order; criteria 18-21 are the file-verifiable things the validator does NOT check (chains_used, the method block, site_pocket_rank carrying both fpocket and prank, and the null-with-a-reason axes). The rubric gates on NO volume threshold: the only numeric volume gates that exist anywhere are the validator's 1000 A^3 merge-artifact ceiling and its 240 A^3 trigger for REQUIRING a tractability.caveat, and neither classifies a target. 207/242 appear in validate_dossier.py only as a comment; VOLUME_GUIDE_HARD_A3 = 210.0 is defined and never referenced. The old criterion 15 ('the final reply carries the dossier') was self-admittedly not machine-graded and is removed from the criteria list — outcome mode shows the grader only sandbox files, so an ungradeable criterion can only produce max_iterations_reached. The reply requirement still lives in CLAUDE.md and is now stated in the rubric's closing section as explicitly NOT a criterion.

NO VAULT — deliberate. mcp_servers is [] and this agent talks to no MCP server, so the starter's vault mechanism (static_bearer credentials keyed by MCP URL, attached via vault_ids) has no code path here. Do not provision a vault credential for this agent by reflex: it would put a live key in cloud-side storage to serve a path that never executes, which is strictly worse than the current position. Revisit only if mcp_servers ever gains an entry. Reasoning and the full credential inventory are in CREDENTIALS.md.

CREDENTIALS: the deployed agent holds no API key and cannot be given one by this deployment. Custom-tool handlers run in the calling process; only tool name/description/input_schema, CLAUDE.md (system), rubric.md (runtime, outcome mode) and the skill zips upload. Handler bodies, .env, acl.ts and fixtures/ never leave the machine — verified against scripts/deploy.ts:166-174 and lib/claude-managed-agent.ts:294,534-536.

PREFLIGHT: tools.ts exports preflight(), called from agent/tools/druggability-dossier.ts before the session is created. It aggregates every missing credential/binary into one throw (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, PAPERCLIP_API_KEY, paperclip/micromamba/modal binaries, the Modal profile, and a live gemmi+numpy import in DRUGGABILITY_ENV). DOSSIER_SKIP_PREFLIGHT=1 is a hand-debugging escape only.

HAND-EDITED SINCE LAST COMPILE, deliberately not re-baselined (second pass, 2026-08-15): tools.ts and rubric.md. tools.ts caught up with modal_app.py's new CLI — pocket_scan now passes --chains (serialised from a {"1TNF":["A","B"]} object into the app's own 1TNF=A,B;2ZJC=A,B encoding), --site-residues, the three paired stage switches (emitting only the --no- form, since all three default true), and --out. The payload is read from the --out file: modal run frames stdout with a banner before AND after the entrypoint, and the entrypoint now writes to stderr when --out is absent, so the old report(stdout) returned banner text and, after the app change, no payload at all on a SUCCESSFUL run. A zero exit with an empty --out file is now a hard throw, because an empty string here reads as a scan that found no pockets. Also: neighbour_precedent and cryptic_analysis accept 4-character PDB IDs through resolveStructure — neighbour_precedent previously demanded a path readable by the operator's machine, which the deployed agent has no way to produce, so that tool was effectively unreachable from the deployed path; and neighbour_precedent gained --multimer, cryptic_analysis gained --exclude. Tool descriptions now carry the three measured silent-failure modes (ligand classification is useless without SMILES and the entry's own mmCIF _chem_comp block has none; unknown is not apo and holo_call(ids)['determined'] is the test; a disorder number without uniprot_accession is the crystallised construct, IRAK4 0.0/284 against 0.1413/460). Verified by executing the handlers, not just typechecking: 1TNF whole assembly gives chains_used [A,B,C], 14 pockets at D=1.6, ensemble volume 153.3-198.3 A^3 (spread 22.7%), druggability 0.11-0.32; the same call with chains {"1TNF":["A","B"]} gives chains_used [A,B], 7 pockets, volume 155.9-156.0 A^3 (spread 0.1%), druggability 0.201.

PROTO-TOOLS PINNED, 2026-08-15 — modal_app.py installed 'proto-tools[mcp] @ git+https://github.com/evo-design/proto-tools.git' with no ref, so the image was not reproducible and any rebuild could silently swap the foldseek/vina code every computed number was validated against. Now pinned to 1e0bd8f5a8f4525eb5e5c736cbf25c1366929e73. THE SHA WAS DETERMINED FROM THE RUNNING IMAGE, NOT FROM HEAD: a probe function was run on the CACHED image (only mounts rebuilt, pip layers reused) and read importlib.metadata.distribution('proto-tools').read_text('direct_url.json'), which returned that commit; the local `druggability` micromamba env reports the identical commit independently. It also happens to equal the default-branch tip today, so the pin changes nothing about what installs — only about what a FUTURE rebuild installs. Verified end to end by rebuilding with the pin: 3 layers rebuilt in ~95 s total and the image now reports requested_revision equal to the pin. That rebuild is already paid and cached in the rafwiewiora workspace, so the next pocket_scan does not eat it — which matters because POCKET_SCAN_TIMEOUT_S is 1800 s for the whole `modal run` subprocess, image build included. Only the dependency/image lines of modal_app.py were touched; the rest of that file is owned elsewhere.

RENAME — PARTIALLY COMPLETED, DELIBERATELY, AND THE REMAINDER IS LISTED. manifest.json `name` is now 'small-molecule-tractability-review', matching the directory name upstream on labrador/main. This is safe locally even though the local directory is still managed/druggability-dossier/: manifest.name is NOT used to resolve anything. loadManagedAgent(name) joins repoRoot/managed/<name> from its ARGUMENT — the literal string in the eve wrapper, or argv for the CLIs — and manifest.name is used only as the deployed agent's API name (deploy.ts:240), the memory-store name (deploy.ts:316) and session titles. There is no `deployment` block, so nothing is deployed and there is no agent-rename or /mnt/memory/<slug> migration hazard. Verified after the change by running preflight() and by loading the agent through loadManagedAgent('druggability-dossier'). WHAT A COMPLETE RENAME STILL TOUCHES, none of it owned here: (1) the directory managed/druggability-dossier/ -> managed/small-molecule-tractability-review/ — already done upstream, arrives in this checkout via the worktree at push time, explicitly not ours to move; (2) the eve wrapper FILENAME agent/tools/druggability-dossier.ts, which IS the router-facing tool name — still the old name even on labrador/main; (3) agent/instructions.md's dispatch entry — already renamed upstream; (4) the four `managed/druggability-dossier/...` keys in compiled_hashes below; (5) the defineState key 'druggability-dossier-session' (cosmetic); (6) prose references in CLAUDE.md, rubric.md, OUTPUT_NOTES.md, CREDENTIALS.md, .env.example and tools.ts. UPSTREAM IS CURRENTLY INCONSISTENT IN A WAY THAT BREAKS DISPATCH, and it is not fixable from this directory: on labrador/main agent/instructions.md advertises a specialist named 'small-molecule-tractability-review' while the wrapper file is still agent/tools/druggability-dossier.ts, and the wrapper filename is what names the tool — so the router prompt names a tool that does not exist. COMPILED_HASHES KEYS NOT RENAMED — ON PURPOSE, and this is the one place the rename is knowingly left inconsistent. The four managed/druggability-dossier/* keys are the merge base the next recompile diffs against, and they are keyed on paths in THIS checkout. Repointing them at managed/small-molecule-tractability-review/* would make every one of them resolve to a file that does not exist here, which silently disarms the hand-edit detection that the two HAND-EDITED notes above depend on — tools.ts and rubric.md carry deliberate hand-edits whose whole protection is that their recorded hash no longer matches. Losing that would let a recompile overwrite them without a merge. So these keys move in the same commit as the directory, not before it. (They are equally stale on labrador/main today, for the same reason in reverse.)
